attributes.description: NTFS $MFT forensic sweep over high-signal Windows directories using the elastic_ntfs_file extension table (requires osquerybeat 9.5.0+ with the NTFS extension). The query uses a UNION ALL of per-directory blocks — one bounded access mode per directory — because the extension table rejects unbounded scans and its glob is NOT recursive (each directory must be listed explicitly). Directories covered: the global Startup folder (C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup), C:\Windows\Temp, C:\ProgramData, C:\Users\Public, C:\Windows\System32\Tasks, and the current default user profile's Startup, AppData\Roaming, AppData\Local, and AppData\Local\Temp folders (C:\Users\Default). Because directory= is an exact, non-recursive match, per-user profiles must be added explicitly: operators should duplicate the C:\Users\Default blocks and substitute each real user name (e.g. C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Roaming) to cover active accounts. Returns both $STANDARD_INFORMATION (btime/mtime/ctime/atime) and $FILE_NAME (fn_btime/fn_mtime/fn_ctime/fn_atime) timestamp sets, plus NTFS metadata: inode, parent_inode, sequence_number, hard_link_count, object_id, security_id, owner_id, ADS presence, and allocation status. active=0 surfaces deleted or unallocated MFT entries; si_lt_fn=1 indicates $SI creation time predates $FN creation time, a common timestomping indicator. Both signals are triage hints only — they are attacker-defeatable — and should be corroborated with the ntfs_journal_events (USN) query.
attributes.query:
-- NTFS $MFT Forensic Sweep
-- Requires: osquerybeat 9.5.0+ with elastic_ntfs_file extension (beats#50641)
-- Each UNION block pins one directory via bounded access mode (directory + filename GLOB).
-- active=0: deleted/unallocated MFT entry. si_lt_fn=1: $SI creation < $FN creation (timestomping hint).
-- Wire quirk: integer 0 serializes as empty string; if you filter active/ads use numeric comparison (WHERE ads = 0), not WHERE ads = '0'.
-- directory= is an exact, NON-recursive match. Per-user blocks use C:\Users\Default as a template;
-- duplicate them and substitute each real user name (e.g. C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Roaming) to cover active accounts.
SELECT
  path,
  filename,
  type,
  size,
  allocated_size,
  inode,
  parent_inode,
  sequence_number,
  hard_link_count,
  active,
  ads,
  object_id,
  security_id,
  owner_id,
  datetime(btime, 'unixepoch') AS btime,
  datetime(mtime, 'unixepoch') AS mtime,
  datetime(ctime, 'unixepoch') AS ctime,
  datetime(atime, 'unixepoch') AS atime,
  datetime(fn_btime, 'unixepoch') AS fn_btime,
  datetime(fn_mtime, 'unixepoch') AS fn_mtime,
  datetime(fn_ctime, 'unixepoch') AS fn_ctime,
  datetime(fn_atime, 'unixepoch') AS fn_atime,
  CASE WHEN btime < fn_btime THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS si_lt_fn
FROM elastic_ntfs_file
WHERE directory = 'C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup' AND filename GLOB '*'
UNION ALL
